analogs.covers: Solo bull: a short-tempered loner that patrols and defends its paths against rival bulls
Bull life: lives apart from the cows, remembers the routes and surges with testosterone in season

solo.headline: A lone bull with a hippo bull's temper and an elephant bull's memory: he learns the migration paths and fights every rival who uses them.

setting.label: The migration paths it has learned, between courtship and nesting grounds
setting.note: A solitary bull roams and guards the regular migration routes. Solitary bulls stay out of the nesting areas unless they have successfully courted females nesting there.

solo.playsLike: Solo you are best played as a bull. Solitary bulls thrive alone: younger bulls and those who want their own matriarchy learn the regular migration paths and fiercely patrol and defend them from rival bulls. You flush with testosterone in the rainy season, bullfights are always one against one, and you win a herd by courting a matriarchy, which may accept a single bull or a bonded pair. Bulls raised as orphans are more aggressive and struggle socially. A solitary cow, by contrast, keeps migrating and seeks a matriarchy, often with a tiny Psittacosaurus as company.

why.text: Solitary bulls “learn the regular migration paths, and fiercely patrol and defend them from rival bulls”. Hippo bulls guard their own trails and stretch of river just as fiercely (official inspiration).
“Solitary bulls, however, can thrive on their lonesome.” Asian elephant bulls also leave the herd and live alone or in loose bull groups.
Bulls flush with testosterone in the rainy season and fight harder, like an elephant bull in musth.
Some bulls prefer solitary lives, “refusing to have competition in courting cows”, and a herd owned by a solitary bull takes no second bull.

solo.summary: Solo spielst du am besten einen Einzelgänger-Bullen: einen Flusspferdbullen mit dem Gedächtnis eines Elefantenbullen. Du lernst die Wanderrouten, patrouillierst sie und verteidigst sie gegen jeden rivalisierenden Bullen. In der Regenzeit kocht dein Testosteron hoch. Bullenkämpfe laufen immer eins gegen eins, und eine Herde gewinnst du nur, indem du um eine Matriarchie wirbst, die einen einzelnen Bullen oder ein festes Paar aufnimmt. In die Nistgebiete gehst du erst, wenn dich dort nistende Kühe angenommen haben. Spielst du eine einzelne Kuh, wanderst du weiter und suchst eine Matriarchie, oft mit einem kleinen Psittacosaurus als Begleiter.
